_meta.title: conviction.py C4 range_extreme -- dead component, 0.0% hit rate across 482 post-fix rows
sources_read: git show 974ca235 (the fix commit the report partitions on)

root_cause.one_sentence: C4 range_extreme computes correctly (session_high/session_low are populated, range_position spans the full [0,1] range) but was calibrated on a MEAN-REVERSION exhibit (bounce AT the range low/high) while the two live trigger families that use it -- BULLISH_RECLAIM_RIDE_THE_RIBBON and BEARISH_REJECTION_RIDE_THE_RIBBON -- are CONTINUATION triggers that structurally fire near the session extreme IN THEIR OWN TRADE DIRECTION, the mirror-opposite polarity, so the threshold is empirically unreachable for 100% of the current trigger taxonomy.
root_cause.classification: NOT a threshold-unreachable-by-construction bug, NOT a degraded/missing-input path, NOT a key transposition (that defect, bars_prior/prior_bars, was already fixed 2026-08-14 by 974ca235), NOT a wrong-input bug. This is a DESIGN-CALIBRATION MISMATCH: the component's polarity rule was written against one historical exhibit (J's 12:35 bounce, a reversal-style entry) and the live engine's two active setups are continuation-style, so the rule and the population it scores point in opposite directions.
evidence_chain: conviction-shadow-report.json degraded_components for post_fix lists ONLY {'structure': 343} -- range_extreme is absent, i.e. NOT degraded, on all 482 rows.

money_range_extreme_probe.py Part 1: score_conviction() fed the textbook 'good' case (call at pos=0.05) scores range_extreme=1 correctly; fed the textbook 'bad' case (call at pos=0.95) scores 0 correctly; fed a missing envelope_high, correctly degrades. The function is not buggy.

money_range_extreme_probe.py Part 2/3: empirical range_position by side (n=512 rows on disk as of probe run, 482 in the exact report-matched population) -- calls (100% BULLISH_RECLAIM_RIDE_THE_RIBBON) span pos 0.336-1.000, mean 0.812; puts (100% BEARISH_REJECTION_RIDE_THE_RIBBON) span pos 0.000-0.445, mean 0.138. The current rule needs calls<=0.30 and puts>=0.70 -- the OPPOSITE side of 0.5 from every observed value.

Mechanism: heartbeat_core.py's session envelope (session_high/session_low, added by 974ca235) is computed THROUGH the trigger bar inclusive (_sess = win.iloc[:trig_idx+1]), and RIDE_THE_RIBBON is a continuation setup -- by the time it fires, price has already pushed toward the session extreme in the trade's own direction, so trigger_close sits near session_high for calls and near session_low for puts.

fleet_ledger_check.finding: 0 conviction rows in ALL FOUR fleet ledgers (risky-1, risky-3, safe-1, safe-3), both pre- and post-fix. _conviction_shadow is called only from heartbeat_core.py's core (safe-2/bold-2) path; the fleet arms (build_shared_signal.py / fleet_executor.py) never call it.

It matches the shadow report's own 'arms': ['core'] field. Flagged for visibility, not scored as part of H2 (H2 is specifically the range_extreme component, which is undefined for arms with no conviction rows at all).

All counterfactual figures below are reported BOTH ways: 'report_matched_482' (dates <= 2026-09-02, exactly the report's population -- outcome-join n=35 matches the report's post_fix_outcomes.n_joined=35 exactly, confirming an apples-to-apples reproduction) and 'live_as_of_probe_run' (512, includes today).

counterfactual_flip_would_change.description: NOT a proposed live change (conviction is fully shadow -- no SKIP_LOW_CONVICTION branch exists in the engine regardless of this component). This answers the task's literal ask: what would re-scoring the 482 rows with a component whose polarity matches the live trigger family (call scores when pos>=0.70, put scores when pos<=0.30) change in the shadow score distribution.

report_matched_482.note: Score can only move up 0 or +1 per row (the current rule already scores 0 everywhere in this population), so would_block can only flip BLOCK->ALLOW, never the reverse -- structurally cannot have blocked anything that currently gets through.

outcome_join_on_the_47_flips.join_caveat: Conviction rows join to real fills only within +-120s (most conviction rows are shadow-scored HOLD-adjacent duplicate ticks with no adjacent order) -- 5/47 is expected, not a data-quality problem.
outcome_join_on_the_47_flips.all_five_are_calls: Structural, not coincidence: puts' totals in this population tend to sit >1 point below their floor when blocked, while calls cluster at floor-1, so a +1 nudge disproportionately flips calls across the line.

bootstrap_ci_mean_pnl.reading: n=5, CI straddles zero -- INCONCLUSIVE, not evidence for or against the polarity flip. Reported because the task asked for a dollar effect with a CI; the honest read is that this population is too thin to say anything.

verdict.classification_per_lessons_c14: DEAD KNOB, translated-but-unapplied subclass: the component is fully wired (not degraded, not a key bug), computes a real value every tick, but that value's population never crosses the applied threshold because the threshold's polarity was calibrated on a different trade shape (mean-reversion) than the live trigger family (continuation). Distinct from the two PRIOR C4 defects on this same component (2026-08-12 startswith('shelf') substring bug on C2, and the 2026-08-14 bars_prior/prior_bars transposed key on C4 itself, per 974ca235) -- this is a THIRD, independent defect on the same axis, and it is a calibration/design defect, not a coding defect.
verdict.reasoning: Conviction has no SKIP_LOW_CONVICTION branch anywhere in the engine (report _meta.armed=false, shadow_only field confirms). Nothing here is proposed for arming. This report is diagnostic: it explains a 0.0% instrument reading and quantifies what re-scoring would look like IF the component were later redesigned, so a future prereg has the mechanism in hand rather than re-deriving it.
